To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) nitrogen limitation can be assessed by sedimentary δ15N values; (2) nitrogen limitation can also be assessed by sediment C:N ratios; and (3) sediment C:N ratios are not useful in lakes with significant terrestrial inputs.

(1) nitrogen limitation in sockeye salmon nursery lake sediments is associated with a decrease in bulk sediment Δ15N; (2) bulk sediment C:N ratios provide a measure of nitrogen limitation; and (3) the nitrogen limitation in the sediments of these lakes may be underestimated by mixing models.
(1) nitrogen deficiency in lakes affects the isotopic composition of the sediment organic matter and (2) the sediment C:N ratio is a sensitive measure of nitrogen deficiency in these lakes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the use of sedimentary nitrogen isotopic and elemental ratios to assess the trophic status of sockeye salmon nursery habitats in British Columbia, and the potential for these ratios to be applied in other lake ecosystems.
the importance of nitrogen limitation to the ecology of sockeye salmon in nursery lakes.
the importance of marine nitrogen inputs to freshwater ecosystems, particularly in the context of nitrogen limitation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nitrogen limitation in these lakes has a strong influence on the interpretation of sediment nitrogen isotopic signatures.
nitrogen limitation can influence sediment isotope signatures, which may in turn influence the interpretation of isotope data in nitrogen‐limited systems.
the nitrogen isotope composition of sediment organic matter in sockeye salmon nursery lake sediments is not a reliable indicator of salmon escapement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
nitrogen deficiency, as indicated by sediment C:N, is a more sensitive measure of nutrient limitation than is nitrogen isotopic composition.
nitrogen limitation in the lakes of the study region is not simply a function of the amount of nitrogen delivered to the lake but also the rate of nitrogen assimilation by phytoplankton.
nitrogen limitation is an important control on the isotopic composition of lake sediments, and that nitrogen limitation is a function of lake size and salmon escapement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nitrogen‐limited ecosystems can be characterized by a suite of sedimentary indicators that may be used to assess nutrient status and the importance of nitrogen sources in lakes.
the use of bulk organic matter isotope ratios in lakes with low nitrogen status may be problematic, and that C:N ratios may be a more reliable indicator of nutrient status.
nitrogen limitation can have a strong influence on nitrogen isotope ratios in lake sediments, and this must be considered in the interpretation of nitrogen isotopes in lake sediments.
